title: Extending 2R-IS Beyond Two Rounds
summary: The two-round initial-state attack supplies too few states in the stated regime; determine whether it can extend further or prove such an extension infeasible.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether 2R-IS extends beyond two rounds when $\mu 2^{r_G}\le 2^{\nu/2+l}$, or prove such an extension infeasible.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of the 2R-IS attack in a duplex-sponge AEAD setting.
parameters: $\mu$: multicollision-size parameter whose smallness obstructs a larger next-round multicollision
$r_G$: paper-specific parameter on the left side of the stated regime bound
$\nu$: paper-specific parameter in the right-side exponent of the stated regime bound
$l$: paper-specific parameter in the right-side exponent of the stated regime bound
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether 2R-IS extends beyond two rounds in this regime, or whether such an extension is infeasible.

citations.label: Generic Committing Attacks: Zero-Padded Ascon is Less Secure than Expected

progress.summary: The source says another-round extension is unlikely because μ is too small to guarantee a larger next-round multicollision. It provides neither a successful extension nor an infeasibility proof.
citation_labels: Nilanjan Datta et al., Generic Committing Attacks: Zero-Padded Ascon is Less Secure than Expected
